Chapter 6: The Destiny Instinct and the Power of Gradual Change
Have you ever caught yourself thinking that certain people, countries, or cultures are just... destined to be a certain way? Maybe you’ve heard someone say, “That country will always be poor,” or “Those people just can’t change.” That’s what’s called the destiny instinct.
The destiny instinct is this idea that the world runs on some unchangeable script, where certain groups are stuck—forever. It can be tempting to believe, because it makes things feel predictable. But the truth? History just doesn’t back it up.
Think about South Korea. Not so long ago, it was struggling with poverty. Fast forward a few decades, and it’s a leader in technology and innovation. Or look at how public health campaigns have completely changed life expectancy in places that once fought constant disease.
What’s the real story behind these transformations? Change doesn’t happen in a flash. It’s a series of small steps—policy tweaks, shifts in habits, tiny wins over time.
So, how do you keep yourself from falling into the destiny trap? Here are a few ways:
First, pay attention to change over time. Don’t just look at a single snapshot—zoom out and watch the bigger picture evolve.
Second, remember that cultures and societies aren’t set in stone. They adapt, they grow, and sometimes they surprise us, especially when faced with new opportunities or unexpected challenges.
And finally, don’t assume the way things are today is how they’ll always be. Nothing is truly permanent.
For example, you might hear the claim, “Africa will always be poor.” But look at the rapid economic growth in so many African cities, or the way mobile banking is transforming lives. Or the old belief that “women will always be less educated”—that’s being proven wrong every day as more girls around the world enroll in school.
When you recognize the power of gradual change, you leave room for hope. You see that progress is possible—even when the odds feel overwhelming. And with that mindset, you’re more likely to support practical steps forward, instead of just accepting the status quo.
In the end, the world isn’t set in stone. It’s shaped by countless small changes, every single day. And that’s a story worth believing in.
